summary: A Network Host Status report covering July 31 to August 4, 1972. It lists the terminal IMPs and hosts that were left out of daily testing because they were intended only as users.

plainLanguage.summary: This is like a school attendance sheet for the early internet. Someone wrote down which big computers were switched on and ready to help, and which ones were not, so people knew where to go.

questions: which arpanet hosts were up in 1972
subtitle: A weekly health check of ARPANET hosts, with a table of which ones answered a test connection.

tldr.problem: People using the early ARPANET needed to know which hosts were up and offering service.
tldr.mechanism: BBN tested most hosts daily through a Terminal IMP from July 31 to August 4, 1972, and tabulated each result as open, dead, timed out, refused or half open.
tldr.outcome: The note also lists hosts left out of testing because they were users only, and announces that these summaries would stop being published.

today: RFC 376 updates RFC 370 and is a snapshot of one week in 1972. The author states that the series was being discontinued.

sections.title: What the Report Covers
sections.content:
RFC 376 reports on the status of most network hosts from July 31 to August 4. It updates RFC 370. The author is Ellen Westheimer of BBN, and the closing note is signed by Alex McKenzie.

Some hosts were excluded from the daily testing because they were intended to be users only. These include the Terminal IMPs in the network (AMES, MITRE, RADC, NBS, ETAC, USC, GWC, NOAA, SAAC, ARPA and BBN) and the Network Control Center computer at network address 5, which only gathers statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: Some computers were only for visiting, not for sharing. They were left off the daily check.

sections.title: The Host Table
sections.content:
The first table gives, for each host, its network address, site, computer, a status or prediction, and who supplied that information. Examples: address 1 at UCLA is a SIGMA-7 with a limited server, address 4 at UTAH is a PDP-10 server, and address 7 at RAND is an IBM-360/65 listed as user only.

A star marks a host not included in daily testing. The UCLA IBM-360/91 offered only a Network Job Service (NETRJS), which the BBN Terminal IMP could not test, so the report assumes that a connection to the NETRJS logger means NETRJS works.
sections.plainLanguage: The table is like a phone book with a note beside each name saying whether that computer was ready to help visitors.

sections.title: How Each Test Is Graded
sections.content:
The second table gives one letter per host for each of five test dates. The letters are:

  • O Open: the host opened a connection and was accessible to users.
  • H Half open: it opened a connection, then closed it or stopped responding.
  • F Full: it said all network ports were in use and closed.
  • R Refused: it returned a CLS to the initial RFC.
  • T Timed out: no ICP completed within 60 seconds.
  • D Dead: the host was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP.

Some sites advertised that their systems might not be available at certain times, and those are marked with a hash.
sections.plainLanguage: Each computer got a letter: O for open and ready, D for dead, T for too slow to answer, and a few more for in-between cases.

sections.title: End of the Series
sections.content: A note says Ellen Westheimer left BBN to return to school on August 4, so publication of these summaries would be discontinued. The author hoped that more detailed survey data from UCLA-NMC would take their place, and points to survey information already available online at MIT-DMCG, described in RFC 308.
sections.plainLanguage: The person who kept the attendance sheet went back to school, so the sheet stopped. Other people were expected to take over the job.

items.label: Open
items.desc: Host opened a connection and was accessible to users.

items.label: 1/2 Open
items.desc: Host opened a connection but then closed it or did not respond.

items.label: Full
items.desc: Host said all network ports were in use and closed.

items.label: Refused
items.desc: Host returned a CLS to the initial RFC.

items.label: Timed out
items.desc: No ICP and connection within 60 seconds.

items.label: Dead
items.desc: Host dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP.
